title: Private complaint vs police FIR - when to choose which route
p1:
Not every criminal case begins at a police station.

Many people assume that filing an FIR is the only way to start legal action. But there is another route that can sometimes be more effective: a private complaint before the court.
p2: The surprising part? If the police refuse to register an FIR, that does not always mean the matter ends there. A person can approach the magistrate directly and request the court to take action.
p3:
An FIR is usually the first step when immediate police investigation is needed, such as collecting evidence or making arrests. A private complaint is often considered when police action is not happening, or when the complainant wants the court to examine the issue directly.

Choosing the right route depends on the facts, urgency, and nature of the allegation. The wrong approach can delay justice, while the right one can move the matter forward.
conclusion: Have you ever wondered why some cases go through the police while others begin directly in court? Which route do you think people should know more about?
